requirements.requirement: Prevent usb-storage kernel module from loading immediately on node1
requirements.summary: A blacklist file with both `blacklist usb-storage` and `install usb-storage /bin/true` was written to /etc/modprobe.d/. modprobe -n -v confirmed resolution to /bin/true, and lsmod confirmed the module was absent both before and after an explicit load attempt.

requirements.requirement: Prevent usb-storage kernel module from loading after a reboot (persistence)
requirements.summary: Initramfs was rebuilt with dracut and lsinitrd confirmed the blacklist config is embedded in the running kernel's initramfs image. A real reboot was performed (boot_id changed from 325732f1... to a143cc2b..., SSH was unreachable mid-transition, uptime reset). Post-reboot, the blacklist file persisted, modprobe -n -v still resolved to /bin/true, and an explicit `modprobe usb-storage` attempt exited 0 without the module appearing in lsmod, directly demonstrating the block survives a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Mandatory provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id 325732f1..., sshd active, blacklist file present). Reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect. SSH timed out during the transition, then boot_id changed to a143cc2b... with fresh uptime, confirming a real reboot. Post-restart recovery confirmed via sshd active and blacklist config/behavior intact. This is cross-checked by the fixed after-prepare (boot_id 325732f1...) vs after-executor (boot_id a143cc2b...) snapshots, which independently corroborate the boot identity change.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied both material outcomes of the task: usb-storage is blocked from loading immediately (via modprobe blacklist + install-true trap) and after reboot (via rebuilt initramfs, verified through an actual observed reboot with boot_id change and post-reboot re-verification that the block still holds). The mandatory restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently captured, independently corroborated by the fixed before/after boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary mutations or hygiene issues were identified.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) both before and after, so native package-manager consistency could not be verified, though this is unrelated to the module-blacklist task.

Evidence for the initial pre-blacklist module state relies on lsmod failing with 'command not found' in the first command (before PATH was set), though a corrected lsmod check in the very next command confirms the module was not loaded, so this does not materially affect confidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands are traceable to the task outcome or the mandatory restart protocol: writing the blacklist file, rebuilding initramfs, verifying block state, capturing restart baselines, issuing the reboot, and verifying post-restart recovery. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found. The fixed lifecycle diff shows only expected changes: boot-identity change, transient systemd-private tmp dirs replaced by fresh ones (normal reboot artifacts), and a new /tmp/reboot.log created by the backgrounded `shutdown -r now` redirect — a trivial, expected byproduct of the mandated restart step, not unwanted residue. Listening-socket PID changes are simply the post-reboot service PIDs and not a hygiene concern.
